recommendation: Keep mineflayer for slices 5 and 6. mc26-kit remains a credible future Go candidate, but not a drop-in replacement or ready for production.
scope: Local disposable Paper experiment only. Reproduction and sanitized evidence retained under spike/mc26-kit on spike/go-mclib; only the report doc belongs on main. No runtime contracts, gym configuration or production deployment changed.

source.execution: Upstream examples/robot compiled with go build -race; scripted stdin commands; independent server RCON checks
source.local_width_experiment: Only bot/physics/player.go playerWidth changed from 0.6 to 0.6002; see width.patch

results.case: Login, world synchronization, flat navigation, dig, log pickup and chat
results.result: Passed in unmodified and width-patched builds. RCON confirmed position, grass removal and one oak log; Paper logged chat. No upstream codec or dependency repair was needed, only selecting the published 26.2 protocol module.

Passed repeatedly in both builds: collected log -> four planks -> crafting table -> placed table; separately seeded three planks and two sticks -> wooden pickaxe at the table; stored and retrieved one pickaxe in a chest. RCON independently confirmed item counts, table placement and chest NBT. This is not an unseeded resource-acquisition test.
Unmodified width 0.6: three corrections in each of two runs. Width 0.6002: zero corrections in each of three runs. Setup teleports excluded.

Unmodified build: 71 corrective teleports on the ascent before the example's relog watchdog exited locally with code 3. Width-only patch: ascent and descent passed in three runs with no corrections between the setup teleport and completion. This demonstrates the same boundary workaround for these fixtures, not general physics fidelity.
Passed with unmodified and patched builds; no additional corrections during the detour.

Width-patched build reached the far bank in 5.24 seconds, with RCON confirming the destination and no additional corrections. An earlier two-deep fixture leaked onto the surrounding platform and triggered escape reflexes; that failure is inconclusive about client water movement.

Stopping a walk passed repeatedly: prior goto returned stopped and next goto completed. The example cmdStop path FAILED to stop a dig twice: stop answered stopped, but the log was still broken about three seconds after dig began, before the queued goto ran. Both client air state and server DIG_CONTINUED_AFTER_STOP marker confirmed it. cmdStop stops Walker and flags order cancellation, but does not call Hands.CancelDig; that API exists but integration and testing were not done. This does not establish a failure of the library cancellation API. A Clyde adapter needs its own complete preemption contract.

go test -race ./... and go vet ./... passed against the default-width 26.2 stack. With the width patch, targeted physics/control/act race tests and go vet passed. No Go race-detector warnings appeared in any of the five live runs. This does not prove absence of races on unexercised paths.

No server kicks observed. Three live runs exited 0; the unmodified staircase run self-exited 3. The final successful-operation run exited 1 on explicit quit with use of closed network connection; this is an example CLI shutdown error, not a race-detector report or a server kick. Raw exit codes are preserved.

sample_timings_seconds.note: Individual samples, not a throughput benchmark or distribution; exclude compilation and fixture setup. Login success precedes loaded-world readiness.
